To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the structure of a co-valent steroid-DNA conjugate reveals that the steroid binds to a Watson-Crick DNA duplex by van der Waals forces, and that the shape complementarity between the sterane skeleton and DNA explains the increased fidelity and affinity of hybridization probes containing bile acid residues.

cholic acid residues seal the termini of DNA duplexes, that the steroid does not interact with the nucleobases but only with the deoxyribonucleosides, that the contacts involve the methyl and hydroxyl groups as well as the sterane skeleton of the steroid, and that this shape complementarity between DNA and the steroid explains the increase in affinity and fidelity observed for hybridization of DNA probes bearing bile acid moieties.
the steroid-DNA complex is stabilized by van der Waals interactions between the steroid's sterane skeleton (and its methyl groups) and the undistured DNA termini.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of new ligands for the binding of DNA and the investigation of their interaction with nucleic acids.
the development of novel, specific DNA-binding agents.
the synthesis of new molecules with a specific interaction to DNA and their application as tools in molecular biology and as new therapeutic agents.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cholic acid residues are sealing the termini and thus stabilizing the complex.
the steroid-DNA complex is held together primarily by hydrophobic interactions and van der Waals forces, with no detectable hydrogen bonds or dipole-dipolar interactions.
the steroid-DNA complex is a covalent and non-covalent hybrid, with the covalent bond between the steroid and the terminal deoxyribose serving to anchor the steroid to the DNA termini.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have found a new way to stabilize the DNA terminus, and that this stabilization is based on a shape complementarity.
we have shown how to make DNA sticky, i.e. how to increase affinity and selectivity of a DNA duplex for a specific binding partner.
the cholic acid-DNA complex is the first structure of a co-ordinate covalent hybrid of a steroid and a DNA oligomer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the binding of the steroid to the DNA is driven by shape complementarity and that it does not depend on any specific interactions between the steroid and the DNA.
the binding of a bile acid to a DNA duplex is driven by van der Waals forces and shape complementarity.
a small molecule can bind to DNA termini without the use of hydrogen bonds.
